For Felix Pankonin , locking and checking all doors and windows around the house has become practically second nature. Sometimes, a hot-tempered lawmaker from the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party shows up on his property. Pankonin's bicycles have been vandalized, and he has received threats that something will happen to his animals. Most recently, his partner was physically assaulted. Pankonin is the project director of educational programs on political issues, Jewish history and antisemitism at the Hillersche Villa in Zittau, in the eastern German state of Saxony . The situation is similar for Keerthana Kuperan, who works as a political adviser at DaMOst , the umbrella organization for migrant groups in eastern Germany. stories.title: In Saxony-Anhalt election, small parties will be kingmakers
stories.summary: The far-right AfD has good odds of winning an absolute majority in Saxony-Anhalt's parliament this state election, enabling them to govern alone. It all depends on whether other parties make the cut.
stories.article_text_excerpt: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5JIs8 Saxony-Anhalt is governed from the state parliament in Magdeburg Image: ArTo/Zoonar/IMAGO Advertisement It's rare that a state parliament election in Germany attracts as much media interest as this one in Saxony-Anhalt . On Sunday, the 1.7 million eligible voters in the eastern German state will decide whether the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party can form a state government for the first time. There hasn't been a head of government who belonged to a proven far-right party in post- World War II Germany — at neither federal nor state level. That would change if AfD lead candidate Ulrich Siegmund were to be elected to this position, since the Office for the Protection of the Constitution in Saxony-Anhalt already classified the AfD as such in 2023. Siegmund's chances of a historical triumph are high: For months, the AfD has been comfortably leading the polls with well over 40% of the vote. stories.article_text_excerpt: Multiple vehicles were struck sparking a fire and sending plumes of smoke into the sky following an Amazon cargo plane barreled off the runaway and crashed at Miami International Airport on Sunday, forcing one of the US busiest airports to close all of its runways.The aircraft overran the runway mid afternoon after heading into Florida from San Juan, Puerto Rico, according to the Federal Aviation Administration.Social media images showed the Prime Air aircraft lying beside a road, near two parked semi-trucks. The plane appeared to have landed on its underside and remained largely intact, despite being engulfed by fire.There was no immediate word on casualties in the incident involving a Boeing 767 operated by Amazon Prime Air, according to the Federal Aviation Administration and Miami International Airport.
